bug_semantics: With OAuth enabled behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy, Temporal UI Server created browser authentication cookies with Secure set from c.Request().TLS, which describes only the proxy-to-server hop. When that hop was HTTP, the access-token user cookies (and later refresh-token cookies when an IdP issued one) lacked Secure even though the browser used HTTPS. An attacker who could additionally steer the UI hostname, defeat HTTPS, serve it over HTTP, and observe a later same-site plaintext request could recover and replay the live credential.
flaw_origin: The original ui-server commit replaced always-Secure server-side session cookies with browser-resident user0/userN cookies containing the OAuth access token and set each cookie's Secure field to c.Request().TLS != nil. That made a deployment-internal transport property control a browser-facing cookie security boundary. The monorepo later imported this already-flawed code, and later refresh/session work reused the same derivation; neither the import nor those extensions are the first root-cause commit.
ai_marker: absent — BIC commit object author is Ruslan <11838981+feedmeapples@users.noreply.github.com>, committer is GitHub <noreply@github.com>, and the complete message is "Store user session in browser (#219)" with no body or Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, or bot-author marker.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c7mm-29xf-mmqp describes the reverse-proxy TLS mismatch, cites temporalio/ui#3806, identifies v2.53.1 and v2.53.2 as the concrete vulnerable/patched boundary references, and lists the formal affected/patched ranges as Unknown. In the validated temporalio/ui clone, `git log -L 87,98:server/server/auth/auth.go v2.53.1` stops at aggregate import c6f84170173eb9e9d82a98fd78faf4adc8af09ed (Import ui-server, #1112), where the file appears wholesale with `Secure: c.Request().TLS != nil`; therefore that import is not the smallest BIC. Decomposing through the public source history cited by the advisory, temporalio/ui-server commit 821cf598371353f1b579dfe1e87aeb3638b041d6 changes server/auth/auth.go from always-Secure gorilla session cookies to user0/userN cookies carrying OAuth access-token data and adds the exact vulnerable expression. Direct parent-tree reads at fca4a6967d9e4fb1c8b1521e185bd70d99ba26d8 and 821cf598371353f1b579dfe1e87aeb3638b041d6 prove the parent instead has `sessOpts ... Secure: true` and lacks both the browser user-cookie loop and request-TLS Secure derivation, while the BIC has both. GitHub's BIC commit-object payload gives parent fca4a6967d9e4fb1c8b1521e185bd70d99ba26d8, human author Ruslan, GitHub committer, and the trailer-free message. Version cross-check: ui-server v2.8.0's server/auth/auth.go already contains the BIC's vulnerable access-token cookie expression; GitHub compare for 821cf598371353f1b579dfe1e87aeb3638b041d6 to the v2.53.1 target reports the BIC as the merge base, and temporalio/ui tag v2.53.1 resolves to 9d5774b15b4b8ff9b4337e8b4a9adffeca34b40e and still contains request-TLS-derived user and refresh cookies. Direct fix 1ed83780edfe2e395048d354976f6487b206b9db (PR #3806) derives one secure flag from the configured browser-facing OIDC callback URL and threads it through user, refresh, session, state/nonce, and clear cookies. Tag v2.53.2 resolves to f30ce6f0211bd3985d0b37b7d1c3fdf27f5c9e92, contains 1ed83780edfe2e395048d354976f6487b206b9db, and v2.53.1 does not; ui-server mirror commit 8876b80b63003688ab736f45ef28885695a4f6db is the later sync of that direct fix, not the direct fix itself.
reasoning: The lifecycle begins in the standalone ui-server history: 821cf598371353f1b579dfe1e87aeb3638b041d6 first couples Secure to the inbound request's TLS state while moving the OAuth access credential into browser cookies. Its immediate parent is demonstrably safe for this mechanism because it forces the session cookies Secure and contains no request-TLS-derived access-token cookie. The 2023 temporalio/ui import c6f84170173eb9e9d82a98fd78faf4adc8af09ed is an aggregate history boundary, so treating it as the BIC would misattribute an already-existing flaw; the advisory-linked source commit permits exact decomposition to 821cf598371353f1b579dfe1e87aeb3638b041d6. Later refresh-token work broadened the exposed credential set but reused rather than originated the faulty trust decision. The flawed tree is confirmed in releases from v2.8.0 through the specifically referenced v2.53.1, while 1ed83780edfe2e395048d354976f6487b206b9db is the causal fix present in v2.53.2. Only the decomposed BIC commit object is used for AI attribution: it has a human author, ordinary GitHub web-flow committer, and no AI trailer or marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
